data.body:
Root cause identified (AC1).

Emitter: the reducer's LINK processor, `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` `process_link`, calls `resolve_ticket_id(raw_target, tracker_dir)` without `quiet=True`. Any replay of a ticket whose LINK event carries a raw ambiguous target prints `Error: Ambiguous prefix ...` to stderr; the reducer then keeps the raw target, so nothing fails.

Input containing `6ed2`: ticket frank-rocky-rat (d52f-823f-894e-499a) has a `caused_by` LINK event (uuid ceae9de7-8992-47c2-855c-60825331adc3, provenance explicit) whose `target_id` is the literal string `6ed2`. Two tickets share that quad (6ed2-1e12-0780-4efd, 6ed2-24e5-6985-4faa). Any close that replays frank-rocky-rat without a valid cache (store-wide reads during the completion verifier) prints the line, which is why it appears in closes whose own ticket never mentions `6ed2`.

Reproduction: copying frank-rocky-rat's event files into a sandbox tracker beside two empty `6ed2-*` dirs and calling `reduce_ticket` prints the line every time; a stack spy on `_resolve_prefix` shows the call chain reduce_ticket -> replay_events -> process_link -> resolve_ticket_id.

How the raw target was written: `_resolve_caused_by_culprit` in `_commands/transition_close.py` returns `resolve_ticket_id(caused_by) or caused_by`, so an unresolvable `--caused-by` value is persisted verbatim. Filing that writer defect separately.

Fix plan: pass `quiet=True` in `process_link` (its documented role: a best-effort resolver over ids the current user did not supply), with a reducer test that replays a LINK to a colliding 4-hex target and asserts no stderr output and an unchanged raw target.
